milestone: Brownie MCP Runtime Safety Policy Finite Closure

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Requires MCP tools/call to pass a Runtime-owned structured safety policy gate in addition to mcp_tool_access and server/tool allow-list membership.
Prevents autonomous agent loops from executing unclassified or mutating MCP tools merely because a model selected an allow-listed tool.
Keeps controlled tool execution bounded by task-pinned Mode Pack policy and Runtime permission checks.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances runtime_permission_enforcement and headless_autonomous_development while preserving controlled_workspace_tools boundaries.
answers.new_capability: Runtime can distinguish explicitly safe read-only MCP tools from legacy, unclassified, mutating, destructive, unknown, or approval-required MCP tools before attempting tools/call.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: The previous MCP policy had mcp_tool_access plus server/tool names only, so a trusted Mode Pack could not express side effects, approval requirements, idempotency, or retry semantics per tool.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: MCP server/tool allow-lists would continue to look like executable authority even when a tool is mutating, unsafe, approval-required, or merely a legacy string entry.
answers.non_duplicative: This phase changes compiled Mode Pack policy and Runtime permission behavior; it does not add a wrapper, adapter manifest, new RPC, or documentation-only verdict.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing tool.execute, task.run, and headless run/resume paths are preserved.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase updates existing policy, Runtime execution evidence, specs, and audits rather than adding a summary endpoint.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: MCP tools/call is attempted only after structured Brownie tool safety policy permits approval-free execution; legacy and mutating policies are denied before server execution.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Autonomous runs can safely use task-pinned read-only MCP tools while future mutation and approval work remains fail-closed.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes MCP-S2 and leaves MCP-S3 through MCP-S7 open before Runtime Release Ready.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: MCP-S2 changes Runtime MCP permission behavior and release audit evidence, so strict review must verify that only structured read-only safe MCP tools can execute and that legacy or mutating tool policies fail closed.

exit_criteria: Compiled MCP access includes per-tool side_effect, approval, idempotency, retry, and legacy_unclassified safety policy.
Legacy MCP string allow-list entries remain readable but are denied by Runtime before tools/call.
Structured read_only, approval=not_required, idempotency=safe, non-prohibited retry policy can execute through existing MCP paths.
Mutation, destructive, unknown, approval-required, and prohibited-retry MCP policies fail closed before tools/call.
MCP-S2 is marked closed while MCP-S3 through MCP-S7 and Runtime Release Ready remain open.
behavior_evidence: brownie-modepack test coverage covers structured MCP policy and legacy-unclassified compatibility input.
brownie-runtime test coverage covers read-only MCP execution, legacy policy denial, mutation policy denial, and S1/S1.1 result semantics preservation.
docs/architecture/mcp-runtime-safety-policy-audit.json records MCP-S2 as closed while leaving MCP-S3 through MCP-S7 open.

accepted_capability: MCP tools/call now requires structured per-tool Brownie safety policy.
Legacy unclassified and mutating MCP tools fail closed before server execution.
behavior_evidence: ModePack compiler test coverage preserves structured policy and fail-closed legacy classification.
Runtime focused MCP test coverage proves safe read-only execution and denial before tools/call for unsafe policies.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime remains the execution, admission, replay, permission, tool, workspace mutation, and completion authority.
Mode Pack structured policy is the MCP tool safety authority; MCP annotations, descriptions, schemas, results, and model output cannot grant authority.
Mutation and approval-required MCP tools remain fail-closed until MCP-S4 approval binding.
non_goals: Does not add a Brownie-specific tool adapter SDK or protocol.

Does not add Streamable HTTP, OAuth, MCP Apps, Sampling, Roots, Elicitation, public registry, automatic install, scheduler, daemon, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, or recursive Brownie invocation.
Does not close MCP-S3 through MCP-S7.
Does not close full CI workflow hardening while workflow update authority is unavailable.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected treating legacy string allow-lists as read-only because tool names alone do not describe safety.
Rejected deriving safety from MCP descriptions or annotations because S3 has not yet pinned and drift-checked annotations.
Rejected executing approval-required mutation tools in S2 because MCP-S4 approval binding remains open.
technical_debt: MCP-S3 annotation provenance and drift checks remain open.
MCP-S4 tool-level approval binding remains open.
MCP-S5 runtime input/output schema validation remains open.
MCP-S6 secret reference contract remains open.
Previously recorded Runtime Release Readiness blockers remain open, including full CI workflow hardening.

runtime_release_dod: Runtime-owned MCP permission checks, tool execution, bounded evidence, replay, and completion semantics.
Task-pinned Mode Pack policy, catalog provenance, and point-of-use Runtime safety enforcement.
runtime_boundary_contracts: Existing tool.execute, task.run, and headless run/resume paths.
Existing ToolExecutionCompleted, ToolExecutionFailed, and ToolExecutionDenied ledger evidence.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: Scheduling, background polling, daemonization, hosted queues, worker fleets, and remote server operations.
external_adapter_responsibilities: MCP server implementation, GitHub/GitLab/Slack adapters, OAuth application wiring, and remote transport hosting.
commercial_solution_readiness: Enterprise tenant management, SSO/RBAC server, admin UI, monitoring backend, billing, SLA, private registry, and certified stack.

next_capability_rationale: MCP-S3 should parse, pin, fingerprint, and drift-check MCP annotations as narrowing-only evidence against this structured policy baseline.
